sections.html:
Hialeah incorporated in 1925 and celebrated its centennial in 2025. The city sits in Miami-Dade County, which means your bill comes from the county's Tax Collector, while your value and exemptions come from its Property Appraiser. Hialeah Park, a National Register site opened the same year as the city, remains the best-known landmark inside city limits.

County offices control most of what a seller touches, so the sections below cover those offices, the dates to watch and the paperwork buyers request.

sections.h2: Miami-Dade tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
Annual notices go out from the Miami-Dade County Tax Collector at the end of October, and online payment opens that same day. Visit 200 NW 2nd Avenue, Miami, or call 305-375-5448. BillExpress subscribers get the notice by email on the mailing date.

The collector only bills. Value comes from the Property Appraiser, reduced by exemptions, and every taxing authority picks its own rate. If the 2026 real estate taxes are not paid before June 1, 2027, a tax certificate may be issued, and the annual certificate sale starts June 1, 2027.

  • Water, road and sewer assessments, such as OJUS, are collected in annual installments. A bill containing one must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold for the remaining lien balance.
  • Discounts for paying early step down each month, with the largest in November.

sections.h2: What Amendment 3 changes for a Hialeah homestead
sections.html:
Amendment 3 won voter approval on November 3, 2026 and starts January 1, 2027. It affects non-school property taxes only. The school board exemption remains $25,000.

Homestead exemption amounts, Miami-Dade
Tax yearUp to, non-school taxes
Through 2026$50,000 (state homestead exemption)
2027$150,000 for residents established by December 31, 2026
2028$250,000 for the same group
2029 onwardAdjusted yearly for positive CPI change

Newcomers who establish residency after December 31, 2026 begin at up to $50,000, and they generally reach the larger amount in their fifth year of receiving a homestead exemption. Federal constitutional limits and implementing legislation shape that rule, so a buyer relocating from another state should ask the appraiser how it applies.

sections.h2: How to file for, keep or lose homestead
sections.html:
• Deadline: applications and documents are due March 1. A late application may still be taken up to the date printed on the TRIM notice, possibly with a $15 fee and a Value Adjustment Board petition.
  • Residency proof: one item is enough, such as a Florida driver license, vehicle registration, voter registration, a W-2 or tax return, bank statements, utility payments or a recorded Declaration of Domicile.
  • Where to file: use the online Application Portal, or go in person to the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1 Street, Suite 710, or to the South Dade Government Center. The phone line is 305-375-4712.
  • Renewal: homestead owners get a renewal receipt in late December, and a property with a deed change gets none.

Leasing the house endangers the exemption. An unreported change can mean back taxes for up to ten years of exempted taxes, 15 percent interest per year and a penalty of 50 percent of the taxes exempted. Tell the appraiser about any change before you advertise the house for rent or sale.

sections.h2: Deed tax for a Hialeah seller
sections.html:
Only Miami-Dade has a rate of its own: 60 cents per $100 on a deed, with a separate 45 cent surtax per $100 that skips any document transferring only a single-family dwelling. The rest of Florida pays 70 cents.

The clerk takes payment when the deed is recorded, and each person on the deed is liable whatever the contract assigns. Quit claim deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are taxed. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not. For recording charges on your closing statement, look at the Miami-Dade Clerk's current schedule.

Request the permit history for your address from the City of Hialeah building department, and look for any permit that is open or expired before you list. Buyers most often ask about roofs, replacement windows, electrical panels, additions and fences.

Work done without a permit leaves a buyer three options: require a permit, require repairs, or lower the price. Some cash buyers will take the house with open items, while a buyer with a loan rarely will. Learn the facts first, then pick your route.

sections.h2: Disputing an assessment or exemption denial
sections.html:
To challenge value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. To contest a denied exemption, take it to the value adjustment board, which accepts the petition 30 days after the denial letter is mailed. The appraiser sends the proposed notice by the end of August, and the late-filing date on it usually falls 25 days after mailing.

Selling is a good time to review the parcel record, since the value and exemptions on it drive both your proration and your buyer's first bill. Check the owner name, the exemptions shown and the mailing address on the tax roll, so notices actually reach you.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Hialeah house
sections.html:
• Agent listing: more exposure and more showings, plus inspection requests and a closing tied to the buyer's loan.
  • Cash buyer: the house is taken as it sits, timing is negotiable, and the price deserves a side-by-side look with a listing estimate.
  • Relative: still a taxable deed event, and the assessment can change if the cap resets.

Whoever the buyer is, get terms on paper, including the date money reaches you and who pays recording and deed tax. File the Miami-Dade tax bill, any assessment notice and permit records alongside the contract.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
Gather the recorded deed, the latest Miami-Dade tax bill and any assessment notice. Pull the permit history from the city. Tell the Property Appraiser about any change in how the house is used, especially if it was rented while homesteaded, because back taxes and penalties are far easier to sort out before a buyer is waiting. If the house carries a water, road or sewer assessment such as OJUS, ask the tax collector how much remains so the closing agent can deal with it.

Once a buyer is under contract, the closing agent orders title work, asks each lender for a payoff letter, and splits the year's property tax between you and the buyer. A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal, though recording and payoffs still take days, so ask for the expected closing date in writing.

If you apply for homestead in another Florida county, cancel the Miami-Dade exemption. Applications can be tracked on a status page, and suspected homestead fraud is reported to an investigation unit at 305-375-3402. The buyer of your house should file a new application, since a property with a deed change gets no renewal receipt.

faqs.a: Miami-Dade County, so the Miami-Dade Tax Collector and Property Appraiser handle your tax bill and exemptions.

faqs.q: What is the Miami-Dade deed tax rate?
faqs.a: 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax per $100. The surtax does not apply to a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: When is the homestead deadline in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: March 1. A late application may still be taken until the date shown on the TRIM notice, and a $15 fee may apply.

faqs.q: What happens if I rent out a homestead house?
faqs.a: The exemption can be lost, and unreported changes can be back taxed for ten years with 15 percent interest and a 50 percent penalty.

faqs.q: When does a tax certificate sale happen?
faqs.a: The annual sale starts June 1, 2027 for unpaid 2026 real estate taxes.
